name: Learning to forgive
description: Seven days on receiving God's mercy and learning to forgive, with room for honest grief, safety, and wise boundaries.

days.title: Forgiven first
days.note: David describes the relief of being forgiven.
days.devotional:
Before we can forgive well, it helps to know what forgiveness feels like from the inside. David describes silence that wore him down, and then the lightness of confessing and being forgiven.

Forgiveness starts with God's mercy to us.
days.prayer: God, thank You for forgiving me. Let me feel the freedom of it today.
questions: Is there anything you have kept silent about before God?
What does being forgiven feel like to you?

days.title: How many times?
days.note: Peter asks how often he must forgive, and Jesus tells a story.
days.devotional:
Peter's offer of seven times sounds generous. Jesus calls his disciples to keep practicing mercy because God has shown them mercy.

This teaching does not require you to stay in danger, hide a wrong, or restore trust without change. You can seek protection and help while asking God to guide you away from revenge.
days.prayer: Jesus, thank You for Your mercy. Give me wisdom to forgive without ignoring what is true or safe.
questions: What does God's mercy invite you to consider today?
What support or boundary would help you respond wisely to a hurt?

days.title: Joseph and his brothers
days.note: Years after being betrayed, Joseph faces the brothers who sold him.
days.devotional:
Joseph does not pretend nothing happened. He names his brothers' evil plainly. Years have passed, and his response is his own; it is not a timetable anyone else must follow.

God can work even after terrible wrongs. Forgiveness does not erase harm, remove accountability, or require renewed contact. If someone has hurt or threatened you, seek help from a trusted person or appropriate professional.
days.prayer: God, help me tell the truth about harm and choose a safe, wise next step.
questions: What do you notice about Joseph naming the wrong honestly?
What would a safe next step look like for you?

days.title: Forgive as you were forgiven
days.note: Paul describes the clothes God's people wear.
days.devotional:
Compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness and patience are pictured like clothes we put on each day. Forgiveness is woven through them.

For deep wounds, this may be a slow process. You can ask God for help without pretending the pain is gone. Forgiveness and reconciliation are different: rebuilding trust takes truth, repentance, time, and safety.
days.prayer: Lord, clothe me today in patience and forgiveness. Let Your peace rule my heart.
questions: Which of these 'clothes' is hardest for you to put on?
What help do you need as you take a patient step toward forgiveness?

days.title: Mercy from the cross
days.note: Even on the cross, Jesus prays for the people hurting Him.
days.devotional:
Jesus prays for mercy while He suffers, and He welcomes a dying criminal who turns to Him. His response shows the depth of His mercy.

You do not have to copy the timing of this scene or return to someone who is unsafe. Bring your hurt to Jesus honestly and ask Him to shape your heart over time.
days.prayer: Jesus, You forgave from the cross. Grow that kind of mercy in me.
questions: What amazes you most in this scene?
What could you honestly bring to Jesus today?

days.title: Letting go of revenge
days.note: Paul shows how to answer evil with good.
days.devotional:
Letting go of revenge is not saying the wrong did not matter. Paul also says to live at peace only so far as it depends on you.

Doing good never means accepting abuse, refusing protection, or preventing a report of wrongdoing. Seeking safety and accountability can be a good and necessary response.
days.prayer: God, keep revenge from ruling me. Help me seek what is good, just, and safe.
questions: What is the difference between revenge and accountability?
Is there support you could seek as you consider your next step?

days.title: A new start
days.note: Paul describes a new creation and a ministry of reconciliation.
days.devotional:
Paul begins with what God has done: through Christ, He invites people to be reconciled to Himself. Those who belong to Christ can carry that message to others.

This passage does not demand reconciliation with a person who remains unsafe or unrepentant. You may forgive while keeping boundaries. Where repair is possible, let truth, accountability, and safety guide it.
days.prayer: Lord, draw me close to You. Give me wisdom about where repair is possible and where boundaries are needed.
questions: Where do you long for a new start?
Where might you need wise counsel before seeking repair with someone?
